Hi Priya / Vikram —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, I want to formalize a short mutual action orientation so we can align on capacity targets, a simple evaluation plan, and a close timeline for reserved GPU capacity. Goal: agree on throughput SLOs and a clear RACI for the first 6 weeks.

Proposed agenda (30–40 mins):
- Quick intros / stakeholder roles (5m)
- Production workload profile & target QPS/TPU equivalence (10m)
- MAP milestones (evaluation window, procurement, reserved pool cutover) (10m)
- Open risks & next actions (5–10m)

I've attached a lightweight MAP spreadsheet (QuantifyAI_MAP_v1.xlsx) that we can edit in the meeting. I also added a starter throughput CSV (throughput_targets.csv) with the sample token/sec targets we discussed — please correct the numbers.

Immediate asks:
1) Can you confirm who owns procurement (billing legal contact) and their procurement window?
2) Please share a sample payload: typical prompt lengths and peak concurrent requests so we can model batch/latency tradeoffs.

Proposed times for the orientation: Tue 2027-04-13 10:00am PT or Wed 2027-04-14 9:00am PT. Which works for you?

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Alex —

Thanks, this looks great. Wed 2027-04-14 9:00am PT works best for us. I'll invite procurement (procurement@quantify.ai) to the meeting — they handle reserved contracts and will want a short SOW and lead time estimate.

Quick answers to your asks:
- Procurement lead: procurement@quantify.ai (they've asked for a standard 30–45 day procurement window).
- Payload: typical prompt is 850 tokens, responses average 300–400 tokens. Peak concurrency is roughly 120 concurrent requests over 1 hour during batch scoring (batch jobs can be serialized to reduce tail).

On throughput: our internal target is 2000 tokens/sec sustained for low-latency inference (95th %ile latency < 250ms) and 6k tokens/sec for background scoring with relaxed latency (we expect batch). Those are rough — attaching a brief CSV with our measured rates.

See you Wednesday. Priya will own scheduling; Vikram (CTO) will join for the throughput/QoS discussion.

Best,
